live_note: Day ten, Friday morning: rechecked, nothing moved. Still no organization named or confirmed as breached through the flaws, so the running story stays PROVEN. Palo Alto Networks' advisory (updated Oct 28) says 'Active exploitation has been observed' against its firewalls' management pages exposed to the internet, naming no victim; the security firm Dream's Oct 26 report of 25 real servers rooted (three in an unnamed US government-affiliated network) is still unconfirmed by any victim or vendor. GreyNoise's 6 successful exploitations (Oct 28-29) were all on its own decoy sensors, from one attacker address. Brandefense's tracker (updated Oct 29) also lists no named victim. America's cyber agency's federal deadline for the Linux flaw Fragnesia, which it says can be chained with the two PHP flaws, is Oct 31. The third flaw, CVE-2026-115560, still has no fix (no new PHP release found). Odds that a named organization confirms a breach by Nov 7 stay at 70%.
